_comment: Advanced AI Workflows — settings.json snippet. Merge these entries into your project's .claude/settings.json. The setup-with-claude skill does this automatically when invoked.

PostToolUse._comment: Auto-trigger hook for gstack-to-plans. Fires ONLY when a Write tool call targets a path under ~/.gstack/projects/. Path filter is strict — must NOT fire on writes elsewhere (REG-7 tests this negatively). The hook surfaces /gstack-to-plans to the user in Claude's next turn; it does not invoke it autonomously.

hooks.command: node -e "const p = process.env.CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT_PATH || ''; const h = require('os').homedir(); const prefix = h + '/.gstack/projects/'; if (p.startsWith(prefix)) { const f = require('path').basename(p); if (/-design-\d/.test(f)) { console.log('[aaw-hook] gstack design doc written: ' + p); console.log('[aaw-hook] Suggestion: invoke /gstack-to-plans to archive this design doc into .advanced-plans/specs/'); } }" 2>/dev/null || true

_merge_instructions.permissions.allow: Append the four .advanced-plans/** entries to the existing permissions.allow array. Do not duplicate entries that already exist.
_merge_instructions.hooks.PostToolUse: Append the Write matcher entry to the existing PostToolUse array. If a PostToolUse Write matcher already exists, add this hook to its hooks array rather than creating a duplicate matcher.
_merge_instructions.scope_note: The PostToolUse Write hook checks CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT_PATH at runtime. It fires only when the written path starts with ~/.gstack/projects/ AND the filename matches the gstack design-doc pattern (*-design-{datetime}.*). Writes to any other path produce no output and exit 0 — the hook does not interfere with normal development.
_merge_instructions.windows_note: On Windows, ~/.gstack/projects/ resolves to %USERPROFILE%\.gstack\projects\. The node -e command handles this via os.homedir() which is cross-platform. The command exits 0 silently when the path does not match — no false positives.
_merge_instructions.debounce_note: Idempotency is provided by the gstack-to-plans SKILL.md itself (Step 3: if destination is identical to source, it is a no-op). The hook fires per-write but the skill exits cleanly on re-run with no new content — satisfying REG-7 sub-case (d).
